sections.heading: What Is a Panic Bar and Why Does It Need Repair?
sections.body: A panic bar, also called an exit device or crash bar, is the horizontal push-rod mechanism mounted across commercial glass doors and fire exit doors. It allows occupants to exit a building quickly in an emergency by applying pressure to the bar, which releases the latch and opens the door without requiring the user to grip or turn a handle. Over time, these devices experience significant wear from daily use, exposure to weather, and physical impact. Common failure points include worn latch mechanisms, broken push pads, misaligned strike plates, failed mounting hardware, and internal spring fatigue. When any of these components degrade, the bar may fail to retract the latch fully, stick in the open or closed position, or produce excessive noise during operation. Prompt repair keeps exit pathways functional and ensures your building continues to operate without unnecessary interruption. Our technicians carry a wide range of replacement parts and hardware to handle most repairs on the first visit.

sections.heading: Common Panic Bar Problems We Repair in Alexandria
sections.body: Alexandria commercial properties see a wide variety of panic bar issues, and our crews are trained to handle them all. One of the most frequent problems we encounter is a push bar that has become stiff or completely unresponsive, often caused by internal corrosion or a broken return spring. We also regularly service bars that have become loose from the door due to stripped mounting screws or damaged backing plates, particularly on aluminum-framed glass doors common in older office corridors near Seminary Road and along the Route 1 commercial corridor. Dogging mechanisms that allow the bar to be held in the retracted position for daytime entry can also fail, leaving a door locked when it should remain accessible during business hours. Additionally, the strike and keeper hardware on the door frame wears down over time, preventing a clean latch engagement. Our technicians assess the full exit device assembly, not just the visible push pad, to identify every component contributing to the problem before beginning repairs.

sections.heading: Panic Bar Replacement vs. Repair: What to Expect
sections.body: Not every panic bar can or should be repaired indefinitely. When we arrive for a service call, our technician evaluates whether the existing hardware can be restored to reliable working condition or whether a full replacement is the more practical solution. Repairs are appropriate when the core housing is intact and only specific internal components have failed, such as a broken spring, worn cam, or damaged push pad assembly. Replacement becomes the better option when the bar has suffered significant physical damage, when critical parts are no longer available from the manufacturer, or when the existing unit is simply too worn to hold a reliable adjustment after servicing. We carry a selection of replacement exit devices compatible with the most common door configurations found in Alexandria commercial properties. Our technician will walk you through the options, explain the cost difference, and let you make an informed decision before any work begins. There are no surprises on our invoices.
